title: Non-Exhaustive Pattern Matching and Option.get Panic
platform_conditions: Scala 2.13 / Scala 3 standard library on the JVM; MatchError and NoSuchElementException are JVM exceptions terminating request handling
security_mechanism: Option.get, head, and Try.get throw on the empty/failure case, so a parsed-and-validated value is assumed present on the strength of a match that never happened -- an attacker who sends the malformed shape causes NoSuchElementException at the guard, and depending on handler wiring the request either dies or, in a catch-all recovery path, proceeds with defaults. A non-exhaustive match throws MatchError for the uncovered case; when the default branch of an exhaustive match grants rather than denies, the unexpected input fails open. Java interop nulls bypass Option semantics entirely: a null returned from a Java method flows into Scala code typed as non-null and detonates later.

source_sink_clues.source: Payload-derived parse results (Option/Try/Either), enums and sealed hierarchies built from input discriminants, and Java method returns that may be null.
source_sink_clues.sink: Option.get / .head / Try.get / .apply on parsed values; non-exhaustive match on input-driven variants; fail-open default branches in authorization matches

tracking_guards: Check parsed values are consumed via match/map/getOrElse with an explicit deny path, matches over input-driven variants are exhaustive with a deny-all default, and null-prone Java results are wrapped with Option(...) before use.
not_candidate_when: The empty case is handled by an explicit deny/default branch, the match is exhaustive over a sealed hierarchy the attacker cannot extend, or the accessor operates on server-constructed values that cannot be empty.
synthetic_safe_example: parseInput(data) match { case Some(v) => v; case None => return }
public_references: CWE-755: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/755.html
CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
